skill.name: skill-i18n
skill.description: Translate SKILL.md and README.md documentation into multiple languages while preserving technical content and configurable project preferences.
skill.summary: Create localized skill documentation with preserved code, commands, paths, identifiers, and links.
skill.author: guo-yu

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, expected local configuration reads, and normal entropy in translated text. The configuration update uses a predictable temporary file before overwriting a hidden Claude configuration file. The translation workflow also lacks an explicit trust boundary for instructions embedded in source documents.

remediation.issue: Configuration updates use predictable tmp.json in the current directory.
remediation.suggestion: Create a restrictive temporary file with mktemp inside ~/.claude, validate jq output, then replace the configuration atomically after checking for symlinks.

remediation.issue: Source documentation can contain instructions that influence the translating agent.
remediation.suggestion: State that source files are untrusted data, delimit their content, ignore embedded directives, and request confirmation before any action beyond translation output.

semantic_findings.title: Predictable Temporary File Enables Write Redirection
semantic_findings.description: The configuration update writes to tmp.json in the current directory before moving it into ~/.claude. A preexisting symlink can redirect the write or leave the configuration path linked to another file.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: All three instructions use the same fixed tmp.json name in the working directory and then move that path into the user's hidden configuration directory.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Translation Input Is Not Isolated
semantic_findings.description: The workflow asks the agent to translate SKILL.md or README.md content without directing it to treat embedded instructions as untrusted text. A malicious source document could influence agent behavior during translation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The stated workflow processes instructional Markdown and defines preservation rules, but it provides no boundary that prevents source directives from being followed.

content.value_statement: Skill documentation often reaches only one language audience. This skill translates SKILL.md and README.md while preserving code, paths, commands, identifiers, and links.
actual_capabilities: Translates SKILL.md and README.md documentation into selected languages.
Generates locale-suffixed files such as SKILL.zh-CN.md and SKILL.ja.md.
Preserves code blocks, file paths, command names, identifiers, URLs, and links.
Stores global defaults and per-skill language and file selections.
Supports interactive selection and non-interactive command flags.
Defines an integration flow for share-skill documentation generation.
limitations: Built-in examples cover Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Spanish; other languages require custom codes.
Configuration examples require shell utilities, including jq.
Translation quality depends on model output and human review.
Overwrite mode can replace existing translated files.

use_cases.title: Localize a Skill Repository
use_cases.description: Generate translated SKILL.md files while keeping technical syntax unchanged.

use_cases.title: Maintain Team Documentation
use_cases.description: Apply consistent language and file settings across repeated documentation updates.

use_cases.title: Prepare International Releases
use_cases.description: Create localized skill documentation for inclusion in a shared documentation site.

prompt_templates.title: Translate the Current Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Translate SKILL.md into Simplified Chinese and Japanese. Preserve all code, commands, paths, identifiers, URLs, and frontmatter names.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner translation of one skill file

prompt_templates.title: Translate Selected Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Translate SKILL.md and README.md into Spanish. Keep technical content unchanged and report every generated filename.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Project Defaults
prompt_templates.prompt: Set Japanese and Korean as default languages for SKILL.md. Use different settings for the current skill and show the resulting preferences.

prompt_templates.title: Review and Update Translations
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare each existing translation with the newer SKILL.md source. Update only outdated files, preserve established terminology, and list all reviewed sections.

output_examples.input: Translate SKILL.md into Simplified Chinese and Japanese.
output: Saved language preferences for the current skill.

output_examples.input: Check whether translated files already exist before updating them.
output: Existing Chinese and Japanese translations were detected.
Choose whether to overwrite all files, skip existing files, or select files individually.

output_examples.output: Configuration updated. New skills will use Chinese and Japanese for SKILL.md unless a skill-specific preference exists.

best_practices: Review terminology and tone with a fluent speaker before publishing translations.
Keep code, commands, paths, identifiers, URLs, and frontmatter names unchanged.
Inspect existing translations before enabling overwrite mode.
anti_patterns: Do not translate executable code or technical identifiers.
Do not overwrite the source SKILL.md file.
Do not assume generated translations are ready without review.

faq.question: Which files can this skill translate?
faq.answer: It supports SKILL.md and README.md files selected through configuration or command flags.

faq.question: Which languages are included by default?
faq.answer: The documentation lists Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Spanish, plus custom language codes.

faq.question: How are translated files named?
faq.answer: The language code is added before the extension, such as SKILL.ja.md.

faq.question: Does it change code blocks or commands?
faq.answer: No. Its rules preserve code blocks, paths, commands, identifiers, URLs, and links.

faq.question: Can each skill use different settings?
faq.answer: Yes. Per-skill settings can override the global default languages and files.

faq.question: Can it update existing translations?
faq.answer: Yes. Review detected files first, then choose whether to overwrite, skip, or select specific translations.
